findings.title: Anti-bribery & corruption controls for account opening

rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 23 October 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🔴 HKMA account-opening controls: All Authorized Institutions should assess bribery and corruption vulnerabilities in account opening; segregation of duties and enhanced controls for third-party agents are explicit requirements, with no source-stated deadline. Hong Kong 🔴 Anti-bribery & corruption controls for account opening 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261022-hkma-brdr-0c7e79396a ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: SME onboarding, Digital onboarding The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) issued a current circular to all Authorized Institutions following cases in which criminal syndicates offered bribes to bypass AML/CFT controls during account opening. HKMA expects a layered, risk-based approach, including proportionate customer due-diligence information, and says inconsistencies may trigger enhanced review or account rejection. Segregation of duties must be applied during account opening, and institutions using third-party agents to introduce or assist clients must implement enhanced effective controls including due diligence, approval scrutiny and management oversight. HKMA also says institutions should consider bribery risk in ML/TF assessments, develop management information and review controls through a gap analysis; it states no fixed implementation deadline. Actions: • Immediately identify account-opening journeys involving branches, staff overrides and third-party agents, and confirm that segregation of duties is applied. • In the near term, assess agent due diligence, approval scrutiny, management oversight and relevant monitoring information against the circular; escalate material gaps and retain the assessment evidence. Source: HKMA circular — Anti-bribery & corruption controls for account opening SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. Watch List • HKMA says the Hong Kong Association of Banks, with HKMA and ICAC support, is developing detailed guidance on measures to prevent bribery and corruption involving staff; monitor for publication.
